newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures turn higher on US labor data.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures turn higher on US labor data.

text.p: IMM currency futures turned higher in reaction to U.S. data that showed the labor sector had moderated slightly in June, traders and analysts said.
U.S. June nonfarm payrolls rose by 217,000, versus average trade estimates of 222,000 and against May's upwardly revised 166,000.

The unemployment rate for June increased to 5.0 percent and gave weight to arguments that the U.S. economy would grow at a more sustainable rate in the latter half of the year. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left U.S. interest rates unchanged on Wednesday after its two-day meeting.
U.S. T-bond traders took the news as a sign the Fed may hold off another tightening at their August 19 meeting.
September yen, which opened firmer, rallied after the data were released. Both dealers and locals became long in fast-market trade, floor sources said.

September popped up near key short-term resistance at $0.008902, which corresponds to 113.50 spot yen, traders said. They said volume was fairly light, with about 5,800 contracts traded in the first half an hour of pit trade.
Currency futures will close at 1200 CDT/1700 GMT in observance of U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday, July 4.
All U.S. markets will be closed on Friday.

September yen continued to advance to $0.008915, which is roughly equivalent to 113.38 spot yen. One trader said the contract's rally through $0.008900 paves the way for a test of the $0.008928 to $0.008930 resistance area in the near term.
The rally in yen spilled into the other futures pits, carrying September marks to $0.5753 and September Swiss francs to $0.6883.
Swiss National Bank (SNB) chief economist Georg Rich said the Swiss franc should remain stable for the foreseeable future despite worries about the euro.
Rich said it "was not apparent how the desire for a timely transition to the third stage of EMU can be reconciled with the requirements in the Maastrict Treaty."

Confusion about the fate of the EMU is expected to drag down September marks in the near-to intermediate-term, traders said. September marks set a contract low of $0.5721 on GLOBEX. Support is at $0.5714, or about 1.7589 spot marks.
September Swiss francs continued to hold above their contract low of $0.6835. September set a 4-1/2-month low of $0.6842. The SNB left the Swiss discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent.

Rich said a recent firming of Swiss money market rates was the result of market fluctuations and not a result of central bank policy aimed at maintaining a specific interest rate level. He reiterated SNB saw no signs of inflation at present despite strong money supply growth.

At 0920 CDT/1420 GMT, September yen was up $0.000065 at $0.008891, marks were up $0.0010 at $0.5745, Swiss francs rose $0.0015 at $0.6879, sterling was up $0.0078 at $1.6800, Canadian dollars were up $0.0012 at $0.7308, Australian dollars were $0.0009 higher at $0.7543 and Mexican pesos rose $0.000375 at $0.122200. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
